text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-9123 - metrics.scrape.failed (severity: P1). 40% of scrape jobs failing across prom-proxy in us-west-2.
priya: acked. oncall here, looking. any known deploys?
jamie: not from infra side. saw a spike in 503s from s3 exporter earlier. linking logs: https://logs.internal/redwood/streams/xyz
alex: I can join — have debugger on the proxy. joining call in 2.
incident-bot: Auto-escalation: PD-9123 escalated to SRE rotation after 5m unacked.
priya: thanks. initial hypothesis: scraper -> prom-proxy -> s3-exporter path seeing 503s causing scrape timeouts which cascade. customer impact = delayed metrics and alerting.
lucas: Confirmed kafka backlog rising on log-ingest too, likely same upstream throttling. consumer lag +12k.
jamie: grabbing prometheus logs from prom-proxy:
```
level=error ts=2026-03-15T12:01:23Z msg="fetch failed" url="s3://metrics-bucket/2026/03/15/12/.." status=503 err="SlowDown"
```
priya: can we temporarily route scrape targets to read-replica or reduce scrape concurrency?
aj: (alex) We can lower scrape_concurrency at the proxy config; patching now to 50% and restarting proxy pod sequentially.
alex: patch applied to prom-proxy configmap -> rolling restart started (kubectl rollout restart deployment/prom-proxy -n monitoring).
customer-ops: FYI, we have a customer ticket (C-9920) flagging missing dashboards. please share ETA.
priya: ETA dependent on whether S3 rate limits clear. mitigation plan: 1) throttle scrapers (done) 2) scale up proxy pods by +2 on canary nodes 3) spin up fallback sampling for high-cardinality targets 4) notify PD if backlog persists.
jamie: scaling proxy +2 (HPA tweak) and enabling sampling for the largest exporters. running: kubectl scale deploy/prom-proxy --replicas=5 -n monitoring
lucas: kafka consumer group offsets show ingestion still backed up, but rate of increase slowed after throttle. consumer group: log-ingest-alpha lag 12500 -> 12600 -> stabilizing.
alex: enabling fallback: add scrape_relabel_config to drop high-cardinality labels for now; patching configmap.
incident-bot: Deploy bot: configmap updated for prom-proxy at 1748500380, rollout progress 40%.
priya: monitoring for error rate and customer impact. set a temporary alert mute for noisy alerts but keep PD for crashes.
jamie: quick check - S3 request logs show a burst from one CI job doing large syncs around 11:58 UTC. flagged IP 10.240.12.9 in internal firewall logs.
alex: I notified platform-team to pause the CI sync job. pinged @platform-team on rotation.
customer-ops: Please add a short sentence we can paste to customers: "We're investigating delayed metrics ingestion due to upstream object storage rate limiting; mitigation in progress, dashboards may be stale for up to 30-60 minutes."
priya: noted. posting update to impacted customers and support now.
lucas: added a temporary consumer-scale: kafka consumers +2 for log-ingest-alpha group. restarting consumers in batches.
jamie: prom-proxy pods finishing rollout, error rate down from 42% to 8% in last 5m.
alex: S3 errors dropping after platform paused the CI job.
priya: good. re-evaluate in 15m. if stable we will close PD and create a follow-up postmortem.
incident-bot: PD-9123 acknowledged by priya.
customer-ops: communicated to customers at 12:22 UTC.
jamie: can someone open a ticket to limit large CI syncs or add rate limits at the platform layer? I can draft.
alex: i'll own the post-incident action to add quota/guardrails in CI.
priya: postmortem owners: priya (write-up), alex (CI guardrail), jamie (proxy config improvements), lucas (kafka ingestion resilience).
incident-bot: PD-9123 resolved (closed) at 12:51 UTC by priya.
priya: closing notes: primary cause = external S3 throttle induced by large CI sync. cascade: S3 503s -> prom-proxy scrape timeouts -> increased retries -> scrape concurrency overload -> kafka/log-ingest backlog. Mitigations that worked: paused offending job, reduced scrape concurrency, scaled prom-proxy + enabled sampling, scaled kafka consumers. Follow-ups scheduled.
customer-ops: thanks team, customers updated and SLA impact assessed as <1hr.
priya: thanks all, creating postmortem doc and linking when ready. :white_check_mark:
